component.name: Blink
component.summary: Edit Markdown with a live preview

description.p: Blink is a Markdown editor for GNOME, built with GTK 4 and libadwaita. It shows a document as source, as rendered text, or both side by side, and it keeps unsaved work safe: changes are saved to the file as you type, backed up for recovery after a crash, and never written over a change another program made to the file.

ul.li: Rendered preview with tables, task lists, footnotes, images from the document's folder and syntax-coloured code blocks
Documents in tabs, which can be dragged out into windows of their own
Find and replace in the source, and find in the rendered text
Focus mode, full screen with nothing but the text
Export to a standalone HTML file or to PDF

description.p: Documents open in tabs, which can be dragged out into windows of their own or moved with "Move to New Window"; a narrow window shows its tabs in an overview. A file that is already open is brought forward, even when opened through a symbolic link, and two tabs of files of the same name also show their folders. Preferences can open every document in a window of its own instead.

Documents export to PDF, set on A4 pages with page numbers, links and an outline, and the HTML export is laid out like the preview, with its images embedded and code coloured for the light and the dark style. The fonts of the preview and of code can be picked, and so can the width of the editor and the preview. The editor shades every other line and highlights the current one.

Text can be copied from code blocks and table cells in the preview, wide tables scroll instead of breaking words, and the header row of a table is tinted. Only the parts of a document that changed are rendered again, and images are decoded in the background. Questions about a file now name it, and a change made on disk to a file in a tab out of sight is asked about once the tab is selected. Files dropped on the text of a document open, and restored backups are backed up again before the old backup is removed.

A font picked in Preferences that is no longer installed gives way to the system font, and backups left by a crash are offered even when another process has taken the process ID of the one that crashed.

The window is rebuilt on libadwaita's own widgets. Editing, the preview and the split view are three toggles in the header bar, and the split view can be picked at the size the window first opens with. Keyboard shortcuts have their own dialog, with a search, and Preferences sorts the style apart from the editor settings. Settings are kept in GSettings; those of earlier versions are not carried over.

Backups of unsaved work can be recovered after a crash every time: about half of them used to be lost, because their record could not be written. Dismissing the recovery question keeps the backup for next time instead of deleting it. Saving a file reached through a symbolic link writes the file it points to and keeps the link. Bold, italic and link shortcuts no longer change the hidden source while the preview is shown, the preview follows a change of accent colour, and the split view button shows an icon that exists in the Adwaita icon theme.
Preview rendering fixes: images, thematic breaks, list and blockquote indentation, embedded HTML, table links and footnotes.
Preferences, zoom, keyboard shortcuts help, drag and drop, and accessibility polish.
